==English==
{{swp}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sent-|id=perceive}}
Recorded in {{inh|en|enm|-}} since circa 1225, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|consentir}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnsentiō|cōnsentīre|t=to agree; to assent, consent}}, itself from {{m|la|com-||with}} + {{m|la|sentiō|t=to feel}} (whence {{af|en|con-}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kənˈsɛnt/|a=RP,GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-consent.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/kənˈsent/|a=AU,NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛnt|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|con|sent}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|intransitive}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To express [[willingness]], to give [[permission]].
#: {{syn|en|acquiesce|agree|approve|assent|concur|connive|Thesaurus:assent}}
#: {{ant|en|disagree|object|oppose}}
#: {{ux|en|After reflecting a little bit, I've decided to '''consent''' to her practising the piano in the house.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet|act=V|scene=i|passage=My poverty, but not my will, '''consents'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|medicine}} To cause to sign a consent form.
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=A randomized clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of canine lacebacks with reference to canine tip|author=T Usmani|coauthors=KD O'Brien; HV Worthington; S Derwent; et al.|journal=Journal of Orthodontics|year=2002|volume=29|issue=4|doi=10.1093/ortho/29.4.281|pmid=12444268|passage=When the patient was '''consented''' to enter the study and registered, a telephone call was made to research assistant}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[grant]]; to [[allow]]; to [[assent]] to.
#* {{RQ:Milton Divorce|passage=Interpreters {{...}} will not '''consent''' it to be a true story.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[agree]] in [[opinion]] or [[sentiment]]; to be of the same [[mind]]; to [[accord]]; to [[concur]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|8|1|passage=And Saul was '''consenting''' unto his death.}}
#* {{RQ:Fuller Church History
|passage=Flourishing many years before Wyclif, and much '''consenting''' with him in judgment.}}

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''to infinitive''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]

{{en-conj|old=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# Voluntary [[agreement]] or [[permission]].
#: {{syn|en|agreement|approval|assent|consensualness|permission|willingness|Thesaurus:approval|Thesaurus:permission}}
#: {{ant|en|dissent|disagreement|opposition|refusal|Thesaurus:disapproval}}
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=6|book=II|passage=All men know by experience, there be some parts of our bodies which often without any '''consent''' of ours doe stirre, stand, and lye down againe.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Unity or agreement of opinion, sentiment, or inclination.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|14|18|passage=And they all with one '''consent''' began to make excuse.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Advice; counsel.
#: {{syn|en|recommendation|suggestion|tip|Thesaurus:advice}}
